change.title: pr-3-flat
change.description: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) silently drops events with no sample_weight
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is `sum(sample_weight)`. Events stored before a project joined the allowlist, or events with no valid `client_sample_rate`, have no sample_weight. ClickHouse `sum` skips NULLs, so those events add 0 instead of 1. Charts for allowlisted projects would silently under-count with no error. event_manager.py:785-787 only sets `sample_rate` when the value is numeric and in (0,1], which confirms that some events have no weight. A fallback such as `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))` would fix it, assuming the Snuba column is nullable. I did not check that.

findings.title: Stale 60s eligibility cache; invalidation helper is never called
findings.body: The allowlist result is cached for 60s, keyed on org and project ids. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but nothing calls it (the option lives in `options`, and the change adds no hook). After an allowlist change, the same chart can switch between upsampled and raw counts for up to a minute. Reading an option is already cheap and in-memory, so the cache buys nothing. Remove the cache and the dead invalidation function. The comments calling it a 'performance optimization' and 'consistent behavior' do not match what the code does. The docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` also says the opposite, that it reads fresh each time.

findings.title: Substring match on the query string misclassifies the discover dataset
findings.body: `"event.type:error" in query` also matches `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and any query that contains that text. Those would get upsampled counts, or sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows that have no weight. It only checks the raw `query` GET param, not the parsed query. The tests cover only the plain positive and negative cases.

findings.title: Alias 'count' ignores transformAliasToInputFormat
findings.body: `count()` becomes `upsampled_count() as count`, so the result key is always `count`. When `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` is set, the other path presumably returns `count()` as the key. Upsampled and non-upsampled responses could then have different shapes. Please confirm this against the timeseries result code. Also, only a literal `count()` is transformed. `count()` with a different alias or other aggregates such as `epm()` stay raw, and a mixed yAxis list gets mixed semantics.

findings.title: Redundant variables and misleading comments, plus trailing whitespace
findings.body: `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a pure alias. `final_columns` is recomputed in three branches even though the decision is already known at the top. Comments such as 'cached result ensures consistent behavior', 'late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions' and 'better query optimization and caching' describe nothing that happens. Whitespace-only lines remain at lines 223, 234 and 278, and the formatter will flag them. The same trailing whitespace is in error_upsampling.py. Compute the columns once at the top of `_get_event_stats`.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: `sentry-repo` is a gitlink to commit a5d2909 with no related change. It looks like an accidental artifact of a nested checkout. Remove it from the PR.

findings.title: Factory helper duplicates event_manager logic, with weaker validation
findings.body: The helper swallows all exceptions and accepts any truthy value that converts to float. Production (event_manager.py:785-787) requires a number in (0,1]. A bad rate in a test would be stored as `sample_rate`, where production would drop it. It also runs for every `store_event`, not only for allowlisted projects. Mirror the production validation or reuse it, and avoid the bare `except Exception: pass`.

findings.title: Test relies on the factory side effect and a real cache
findings.body: The expected count of 10 depends on the new factory hook that sets `sample_rate`, and on Snuba deriving sample_weight from it. Only `options` is mocked, so the `cache` is real. Cached eligibility keyed on project ids could leak between tests if ids repeat. The unit tests never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the cache path is uncovered. Nothing tests top_events, or the discover dataset with `event.type:error`. `self.user` is also reassigned after `login_as`, which is confusing.

contracts.action: Transform count() to upsampled_count() in events-stats for allowlisted projects
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing timeseries_query path with the unchanged query_columns
contracts.before_after: Before, columns went straight to timeseries_query. Now columns are rewritten when all projects are allowlisted and the dataset is errors, or discover with event.type:error in the query.
contracts.visible_effect: Charts show sum(sample_weight) counts instead of raw counts.
contracts.failure_mode: Events without sample_weight count as 0. Eligibility is cached for 60s and never invalidated.

summary:
Error upsampling for events-stats has these problems:

- `sum(sample_weight)` under-counts events that have no sample_weight.
- The 60s eligibility cache is stale after allowlist changes, and its invalidation function is never called.
- The discover check is a substring match on the raw query string.
- The count alias may differ from the other path when `transformAliasToInputFormat` is set.
- A stray `sentry-repo` submodule gitlink was committed.
- The endpoint code has redundant variables, misleading comments and trailing whitespace.
